haemophilia.title: Understanding Bleeding Disorders
haemophilia.lead: Key information on symptoms, types of clotting factor deficiencies, emergency care, and treatment guidance.
haemophilia.warningText: Head trauma, severe abdominal pain, or acute joint swelling require immediate hospital treatment and factor concentrate replacement.

typeA.title: Haemophilia A
typeA.subtitle: Factor VIII Deficiency
typeA.desc: The most common type of hemophilia, caused by insufficient clotting Factor VIII. Patients experience spontaneous or prolonged bleeding in joints, muscles, and soft tissues.

typeB.title: Haemophilia B
typeB.subtitle: Factor IX Deficiency (Christmas Disease)
typeB.desc: Caused by a deficiency of clotting Factor IX. Symptoms mirror Haemophilia A, requiring specialized factor concentrate management.

vwd.title: Von Willebrand Disease (VWD)
vwd.subtitle: VWD Deficiency
vwd.desc: The most frequent inherited bleeding condition globally, affecting both males and females due to low or defective von Willebrand Factor.

rare.title: Rare Clotting Deficiencies
rare.subtitle: Factors II, V, VII, X, XI, XIII
rare.desc: Rare plasma protein deficiencies that disrupt normal coagulation cascades. Each requires targeted diagnostic panel screening.

faqs.a1: Haemophilia is a hereditary genetic condition that hinders normal blood clotting due to a deficiency in key clotting proteins.
faqs.q2: How is it treated in Cambodia?
faqs.a2: Treatment relies on factor concentrate replacement therapy, fresh plasma transfusions, and specialized care at partner treatment centers.
faqs.a3: While standard treatment manages symptoms effectively, advanced clinical research in gene therapy is showing major curative breakthroughs worldwide.
faqs.a4: Yes! With early diagnosis, routine prophylaxis, and emergency care access, patients can safely participate in school, work, and community life.
